append_boundary_checks.readiness_equality_policy: Field-for-field equality of complete owner-typed tuples; no field subset, digest-only reduction, omitted/null member or extra/missing family/sample entry. Operational value equality is an additional check. Start-authority is a separate event-payload tuple, never a readiness nested field.
append_boundary_checks.transaction_policy: Every append uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE; fix as_of once after acquiring the writer lock; resolve and check currentness against one stable synthetic catalog snapshot; inspect committed state and append in that transaction; any refusal rolls back event, head, origin allocation and capability changes. Catalog mutations must serialize with this snapshot through commit.

stage3_sample_bundle.roles: Same sample reviewer/producer/envelope separation and private-input-producer exclusion as SAMPLE_REGISTERED
stage3_sample_bundle.failure_policy: Missing, stale, superseded, revoked, noncurrent or mismatched evidence refuses before append; no resolver-hit shortcut.

inventory_seal_roles.source_policy: These are v7 semantic field bindings on resolved bytes, not caller role labels. Design PR must freeze their owner-schema paths; missing/ambiguous paths block runtime admission. Seal-authority issuer and envelope actor may coincide if that authority explicitly binds the actor; no equality waives the listed prohibitions.

origin_invariant.scope: One ledger epoch across all campaigns; never reset by a campaign, local sample ID, acceptance generation or projection change.
origin_invariant.canonical_lineage_source: Required safe_public_id canonical_sample_lineage_id from resolved complete sample-record bytes on BOTH local and Stage 3 paths; local schema must expose it before admission; never derive it from sample_id or trust request-only text.
origin_invariant.record_identity_source: Complete owner-typed authority/record identity tuple from resolved record key; compare every identity field. Mutable acceptance/publication generations are not record identity.
rules: At most one origin allocation, representation path and local sample_id for each lineage and for each authority/record identity tuple.
At both origin boundaries search committed origins of both event types for tuple and lineage matches before insertion.
Same tuple independently forbids another identity, even if lineage claim differs. Different tuple does not permit another identity for the same lineage.
Existing local/external path cannot be replaced or supplemented through the other origin event; replay or same sample_id is not a new allocation.
Check and insertion share the writer-locked transaction; two competing connections cannot both commit.
CAMPAIGN_ENTITY_BOUND is a later reference to the existing sample_id and pinned origin; it creates no origin and does not reserve another lineage slot.
origin_invariant.later_reference_conditions: Committed target campaign sequence strictly greater than origin campaign sequence; original tuple and source hashes unchanged; no direct-scope/binding mixture; current sample/family bundles.

positive_controls: Path A first checkpoint through ACCESS_INTENT then ACCESS_STARTED with valid synthetic catalog; stop before ACCESS_COMPLETED because EXPOSURE_DECISION is not selected.
Path B starts exactly once when every readiness operand and operational value equals the same-transaction result.
Each origin path succeeds separately in a fresh epoch with current evidence and separated roles.
A legitimate later-campaign CAMPAIGN_ENTITY_BOUND reuses the existing sample_id without creating an origin.
Readiness executor, different from start-event actor, can consume matching EXECUTE capability after committed start.
negative_case_oracle: Begin with a passing synthetic fixture for that boundary. Introduce only the stated fault, with all earlier gates valid. Require the named refusal and zero committed event/head/origin/capability changes except the winning concurrent append. Recompute fixture digests so schema/hash failure does not mask the intended predicate. For overlapping tuple and lineage guards, also assert each guard independently on the resolved bundle; removing one guard need not make the full append succeed when another mandatory guard still rejects it.
